I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for over twenty years. My father farmed it before me. The answer is simple: wheat in winter, maize in summer. That's what this land is for. That's what the grain station buys. That's what my neighbors grow. I have about 8 mu, and every mu goes into that rotation — I'm not going to gamble on vegetables or anything exotic. I don't have the connections to sell them and I don't want the risk.

For the wheat, I'll use Jimai 22 — it's what the seed shop sells most of, it performs well here, and I've used it before. I'll rotary-till before planting. Fertilizer: I put down diammonium phosphate and urea as base, then top-dress urea at jointing. I irrigate at wintering, jointing, and heading — three times. Aphids and powdery mildew show up every year so I'll spray twice. I expect around 450 jin per mu — about 450 kg if conditions are decent.

For maize, I go straight into the stubble right after wheat harvest in June, no time to waste. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed — it's reliable and cheap enough. I don't bother ploughing, just direct seed. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress urea at V6 and tasseling. Rain is usually enough in summer but I'll pump once if it gets dry in August. One pesticide pass for fall armyworm if I see it. Maize usually gives me 550–600 kg per mu.

Nothing fancy. I know this system. It works.
